output.methodChoice: EDF sequence with two collected items: X12 (Corvane edge event log) and X11 (Android outcomes by version, OS and outcome category). Both were chosen because they directly test the edge-layer rival and the app-release rival.
output.brief:
The Android password-login drop is mainly caused by a new vendor rule, not by release 6.14 or by attackers. On 3 March at 10:38 UTC Corvane's automatic rule-pack update (2026.03.1) added rule AUTO-LIB-17, which blocks requests with the 'nettle-http' user-agent on the password path. Blocks began at 10:41 UTC, and the Android password failures are all HTTP 403 server rejections that start within a minute on every app version. The blocked requests come from real installed apps, 92% with earlier successful logins. iOS, web and quick-unlock are unaffected. Confidence is high, though I did not check the 6.14 rollout's own network traffic or the contact-centre link.

Next steps: ask Corvane to set AUTO-LIB-17 to log-only on the mobile password path, keeping rate limits and lockout, and confirm recovery in telemetry. Do not raise bot sensitivity or drop blocked attempts from the KPI; both would worsen the lockout or hide it. Hold the password-screen revert and the rollback plan until this is confirmed.
